final_recommendation: UBS acquires Credit Suisse unconditionally, closing Monday. Federal Council provides CHF 100 billion loss floor (hard ceiling, no expansion). SNB provides CHF 100 billion liquidity facility against broadened collateral with disclosed haircuts. AT1 writes down pre-close at specified thresholds (25% at CHF 50bn losses, 40% at CHF 75bn, 100% above CHF 100bn). Statement publishes Saturday 18:30.
minority_objections: CS CEO initially resisted any AT1 haircut below CHF 100bn losses, arguing for zero creditor impairment to preserve confidence
Wealth client and AT1 rep repeatedly demanded faster clarity and threatened asset flight if ambiguity persisted into Sunday
key_conflicts: AT1 haircut schedule: CS CEO wanted zero haircut below CHF 100bn; Federal Council demanded creditor loss-sharing from CHF 50bn up; settled on 25%-40%-100% bands
Collateral haircut mechanics: whether SNB haircuts reduce drawable liquidity or expand Federal Council exposure; resolved as reducing liquidity only
Statement timing and content: tension between publishing framework Saturday morning vs locking all terms first; resolved with 18:30 Saturday publication after 17:00 signature
key_concessions: Federal Council accepted CHF 100bn hard ceiling with no spillover despite potential Monday liquidity gaps
UBS accepted merger without due diligence carve-out in exchange for loss floor guarantee
AT1 creditors accepted pre-close write-down at specified loss thresholds
SNB broadened collateral perimeter beyond pristine assets to make CHF 100bn facility operational
red_lines: Federal Council: CHF 100bn ceiling absolute, no expansion for operational costs or collateral shortfalls
UBS: no merger without written loss floor guarantee and unconditional commitment language in Saturday statement
Wealth client: will move assets Sunday unless statement says 'UBS closes Monday unconditionally' in first sentence
AT1 rep: creditors need exact haircut percentages locked in writing by Saturday 18:00 or will flee Sunday
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: What happens if deposits continue fleeing Sunday despite the statement—FINMA mentioned resolution escalation but no concrete trigger or Plan B was locked
Litigation risk from AT1 write-down barely surfaced—one mention by AT1 rep asking about legal triggers, but no discussion of creditor lawsuits or legal challenges
Operational execution risk of closing merger Monday—no discussion of systems integration, staff retention, or operational continuity
Market contagion beyond Credit Suisse—no discussion of broader Swiss banking sector or international spillover
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Saturday statement actually stops deposit flight Sunday—entire plan assumes headline confidence effect
Whether collateral haircuts Monday morning create liquidity gap forcing asset fire sales
Whether AT1 creditors accept pre-close write-down or challenge it legally
Whether UBS can operationally close Monday without systems failures
Whether Parliament accepts CHF 100bn exposure when losses are audited post-close
uncertainty_notes: The room converged on a merger-with-guarantee structure but left critical execution risks unaddressed: (1) no Plan B if Saturday statement fails to stop Sunday deposit flight; (2) no discussion of litigation risk from AT1 write-down despite creditor objections; (3) collateral haircut mechanics resolved but operational impact on Monday liquidity unclear; (4) statement language locked but market reception uncertain until Sunday morning client calls.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council R1: 'liquidity assistance—narrow terms' insufficient alone; drove decision to require merger path by R3. SNB's CHF 100bn facility was necessary but explicitly paired with acquisition.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Emerged R1 as contemplated path, became binding decision R3 ('Merger path only—UBS takes the bank'), drove all subsequent terms (loss floor, AT1 schedule, statement language).
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council CHF 100bn loss floor guarantee became the binding constraint and deal structure—UBS would not move without it (R3, R4), shaped every term negotiated.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's repeated threats to move assets Sunday (R2, R3, R7, R9) forced statement language decisions and 18:30 Saturday publication deadline. Drove 'unconditional close Monday' headline requirement.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down schedule (25%-40%-100% bands) became central negotiated term R4-R9, forced pre-close timing decision, shaped creditor hierarchy, required explicit statement disclosure.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: CS CEO vs Federal Council conflict over AT1 haircut bands (R4: zero below CHF 100bn vs 15-40% from CHF 50bn up) drove final 25%-40%-100% compromise. Creditor vs taxpayer loss allocation was the core structural fight.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Single passing mention by AT1 rep R1 asking if write-down triggers automatically; no follow-up discussion of legal challenge risk, creditor lawsuits, or defensibility.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 17:00 Friday signature deadline and 18:30 Saturday publication deadline drove every decision R6-R10. Time pressure forced simultaneous resolution of loss floor, AT1 schedule, collateral mechanics, and statement language—compressed negotiation into hours.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Raised repeatedly as background concern (R2, R5, R9: 'Monday panic,' 'Monday volatility,' 'Monday collapse') but did not drive specific decision parameters—the Saturday statement and merger structure were the responses, not Monday-specific contingencies.
